title: A water board's maintenance share

blocks.text: A regional water board picks this year's capital projects. Each project is `"maintenance"` (renewing pipes and pumps that exist) or `"growth"` (new capacity), with a cost in $k. The model in `board.py` has a binary `x[pid]` per project. The board's rules:

items: **Use it.** The plan spends at least the share `use` of the budget: a plan that leaves too much unspent will cost the board its funding next year.
**Maintenance band.** Maintenance makes up between the share `low` and the share `high` of what the plan actually spends.

blocks.text: Write `add_spend_rules(model, x, projects, budget, use, low, high)` so that the model allows exactly the plans that keep the three rules.
The model so far, with $`P`$ the projects:

Name the parameters and write the plan's spend and its maintenance spend as expressions first. The band is a ratio of two of your expressions; write each of its two rows so that it is linear, with its label, before you code it.
The tests fix every `x[pid]` through its bounds and ask the solver whether the model accepts the plan, so any correct formulation passes. About eight lines.

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

from ortools.math_opt.python import mathopt


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Project:
    pid: str
    kind: str          # "maintenance" or "growth"
    cost: int


def add_spend_rules(model: mathopt.Model, x: dict, projects: list[Project], budget: int, use: float,
                    low: float, high: float) -> None:
    """Spend between use x budget and budget; maintenance between low and high of the plan's spend."""
    total = sum(p.cost * x[p.pid] for p in projects)
    upkeep = sum(p.cost * x[p.pid] for p in projects if p.kind == "maintenance")
    model.add_linear_constraint(total <= budget, name="budget")
    model.add_linear_constraint(total >= use * budget, name="use_it")
    model.add_linear_constraint(upkeep >= low * total, name="upkeep_low")
    model.add_linear_constraint(upkeep <= high * total, name="upkeep_high")


def build(projects: list[Project], budget: int, use: float, low: float,
          high: float) -> tuple[mathopt.Model, dict]:
    model = mathopt.Model(name="water-board")
    x = {p.pid: model.add_binary_variable(name=f"x_{p.pid}") for p in projects}
    add_spend_rules(model, x, projects, budget, use, low, high)
    return model, x


if __name__ == "__main__":
    projects = [Project("PIPE", "maintenance", 300), Project("TANK", "growth", 500)]
    model, x = build(projects, 900, 0.8, 0.3, 0.5)
    print(model.get_num_linear_constraints(), "rows")

cases.says: a plan between the floor and the budget is allowed, and one below the floor or over the budget is refused
a plan whose maintenance share is too low or too high is refused
a plan that spends less needs proportionally less maintenance
maintenance under half the budget is still refused when it is over half of what the plan spends

origin.section: A Share of the Plan Is Linear Once You Multiply Out the Total

concepts: a share of the plan's spend becomes linear once both sides are multiplied by the total
a ceiling and a floor are rows on the same spend expression, and a floor makes the model fund work for its spend
